assignedReviews.card_evidence: What happened to the finches when a drought hit their islands in 1977?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about drought effects on finch populations and natural selection, with no mention of protons, neutrons, electrons, or atomic structure. It does not support the competency in any way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What happened to the finches when a drought hit their islands in 1977?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses finch survival during drought, not the structure of an atom or electron shells. It is entirely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
What happened to the finches when a drought hit their islands in 1977?

The finch population decreased by 85% because food decreased, and only birds with beaks for the remaining hard seeds survived.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyari sa mga finch nang tumama ang drought sa kanilang mga isla noong 1977?

Bumaba ang population ng finch ng 85% dahil bumaba ang pagkain, at tanging mga ibon na may tuka para sa natitirang matitigas na buto ang nabuhay.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nahitabo sa mga finch sa dihang miigo ang hulaw sa ilang mga isla niadtong 1977?

Ang population sa finch mikunhod og 85% tungod kay mikunhod ang pagkaon, ug ang mga langgam lamang nga adunay sungo alang sa nahabilin nga gahi nga mga liso ang naluwas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Drying fish or meat removes water, which slows down the growth of microorganisms like bacteria, yeast, and molds that spoil food.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about food preservation by drying and its effect on microorganisms. It does not describe photosynthesis or respiration, nor their raw materials and products. The assigned competency is unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: Drying fish or meat removes water, which slows down the growth of microorganisms like bacteria, yeast, and molds that spoil food.
copy.tl: Ang pagpapatuyo ng isda o karne ay nag-aalis ng tubig, na nagpapabagal sa pagdami ng mga microorganism tulad ng bacteria, yeast, at molds na sumisira ng pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang pagpauga sa isda o karne nagtangtang sa tubig, nga nagpahinay sa pagdaghan sa mga microorganism sama sa bacteria, yeast, ug molds nga makadaot sa pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fishermen can dry their catch immediately under the sun to preserve the fish for a longer time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sun-drying fish for preservation, which has no connection to homeostasis, body systems, or their indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fishermen can dry their catch immediately under the sun to preserve the fish for a longer time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address feedback mechanisms, positive or negative, that maintain homeostasis. It is about food preservation, not human physiology.

copy.en: Fishermen can dry their catch immediately under the sun to preserve the fish for a longer time.
copy.tl: Maaaring patuyuin agad ng mga mangingisda ang kanilang mga nahuling isda sa ilalim ng araw para mapreserba ito nang mas matagal.
copy.bis: Mahimo dayon nga paugahon sa mga mangingisda ang ilang mga nadakpan nga isda ilalom sa adlaw aron mapreserbar kini sa mas taas nga panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light has a dual nature, meaning it behaves like a wave in some situations and like a particle in others.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Wave–particle duality of light is optics, not plant reproduction.

copy.en:
Can light be both a wave and a particle?

Yes! Light has a dual nature, meaning it behaves like a wave in some situations and like a particle in others.
copy.tl:
Pwede bang maging wave at particle ang liwanag?

Oo! May dual nature ang liwanag, ibig sabihin kumikilos ito bilang wave sa ilang pagkakataon at bilang particle naman sa iba.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang wave ug particle ang kahayag?

Oo! Ang kahayag adunay dual nature, nagpasabot nga molihok kini isip wave sa pipila ka sitwasyon ug isip particle sa uban.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During a typhoon, stay indoors
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about typhoon safety precautions, which is unrelated to using a microscope to observe cell parts. The assigned competency G7-L-2 concerns microscope techniques and cell organelles, so the tag is incorrect.

copy.en: During a typhoon, stay indoors, keep updated with the latest weather report, and turn off electricity if water starts to rise.
copy.tl: Sa panahon ng bagyo, manatili sa loob ng bahay, makinig sa pinakabagong ulat panahon, at patayin ang kuryente kung tumataas na ang tubig.
copy.bis: Sa panahon sa bagyo, pagpabilin sa balay, paminaw sa pinakabag-o nga balita sa panahon, ug palonga ang kuryente kung mosaka na ang tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dwarf planets each have a rocky core surrounded by a thick layer of ice
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: Card describes dwarf planet composition; no information about plate boundaries, their structures, movements, or events.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dwarf planets each have a rocky core surrounded by a thick layer of ice
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: Card discusses dwarf planets, not volcano types, activity, eruption type, or crustal location.

copy.en: Dwarf planets each have a rocky core surrounded by a thick layer of ice, and they are smaller than Earth's moon.
copy.tl: Ang bawat dwarf planet ay may mabatong core na napapalibutan ng makapal na layer ng yelo, at mas maliit sila kaysa sa buwan ng Earth.
copy.bis: Ang matag dwarf planet adunay batoon nga core nga gilibotan sa baga nga layer sa yelo, ug mas gagmay sila kaysa sa bulan sa Earth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists estimate there are only about 180 to 500 Philippine eagles left in the wild.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a population estimate for Philippine eagles. G10-L-1 requires describing homeostasis as a state of balance among human body systems with indicators like body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure. The card provides no information about homeostasis or human body systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists estimate there are only about 180 to 500 Philippine eagles left in the wild.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: G10-L-2 requires explaining how homeostasis is maintained through positive and negative feedback mechanisms. The card is about an eagle population count and contains no content on feedback mechanisms or homeostasis.

copy.en: Scientists estimate there are only about 180 to 500 Philippine eagles left in the wild.
copy.tl: Tinataya ng mga siyentista na mayroon lamang mga 180 hanggang 500 Philippine eagle ang natitira sa wild.
copy.bis: Gibanabana sa mga siyentista nga aduna lamang mga 180 hangtod 500 ka Philippine eagle ang nahibilin sa wild.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ear is the sense organ we use for hearing
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the ear as a sense organ for hearing, which is unrelated to the competency's focus on outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their roles in movement and food gathering. The ear is not an outer body part used for locomotion or feeding, so the card does not support this competency.

copy.en: The ear is the sense organ we use for hearing — one of our five amazing senses!
copy.tl: Ang tainga ang sense organ na ginagamit natin para makarinig — isa sa ating limang pandama!
copy.bis: Ang dalunggan mao ang sense organ nga gigamit nato sa pagdungog — usa sa atong lima ka sentido!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth Hour is a worldwide movement organized by the World Wildlife Fund to encourage people to turn off lights for one hour to save energy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Earth Hour, an energy-saving campaign, which has no connection to identifying landforms, bodies of water, or their influence on environmental components as required by G5-E-1.

copy.en: Earth Hour is a worldwide movement organized by the World Wildlife Fund to encourage people to turn off lights for one hour to save energy.
copy.tl: Ang Earth Hour ay isang pandaigdigang kilusan na inorganisa ng World Wildlife Fund upang hikayatin ang mga tao na patayin ang mga ilaw sa loob ng isang oras upang makatipid ng enerhiya.
copy.bis: Ang Earth Hour usa ka tibuok kalibutan nga kalihukan nga giorganisar sa World Wildlife Fund aron awhagon ang mga tao sa pagpalong sa mga suga sa usa ka oras aron makatipid ug enerhiya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's grid or coordinate system uses imaginary reference lines, like latitude, to determine the exact location of any place on the surface.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Earth's grid/coordinate system and latitude, which is unrelated to changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) or diagrams/flowcharts of those processes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's grid or coordinate system uses imaginary reference lines, like latitude, to determine the exact location of any place on the surface.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about Earth's coordinate system, not about the role of heat energy in change of state processes. No connection to the competency.

copy.en: Earth's grid or coordinate system uses imaginary reference lines, like latitude, to determine the exact location of any place on the surface.
copy.tl: Ang grid o coordinate system ng Earth ay gumagamit ng mga imaginary reference lines, tulad ng latitude, para matukoy ang eksaktong lokasyon ng anumang lugar sa surface.
copy.bis: Ang grid o coordinate system sa Earth naggamit og imaginary reference lines, sama sa latitude, aron matino ang eksaktong lokasyon sa bisan unsang lugar sa surface.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth formed on January 1
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the compressed timeline of Earth's history and the Precambrian, with no mention of electricity, electron flow, or electrical safety. It does not support the competency in any way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth formed on January 1
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about Earth's geological history, not about energy causing change or light, sound, and heat energy. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
What if Earth's whole history was squeezed into one year?

Then Earth formed on January 1, and the first life appeared in late March, showing how incredibly long the Precambrian was!
copy.tl:
Paano kung ang buong kasaysayan ng Daigdig ay isiksik sa isang taon?

Kung gayon, nabuo ang Daigdig noong Enero 1, at ang unang buhay ay lumitaw noong huling bahagi ng Marso, na nagpapakita kung gaano kahaba ang Precambrian!
copy.bis:
Unsa kaha kon ang tibuok kasaysayan sa Yuta ipislit sa usa ka tuig?

Nan ang Yuta naporma sa Enero 1, ug ang unang kinabuhi mitungha sa ulahing bahin sa Marso, nga nagpakita kung unsa ka taas ang Precambrian!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Epicenters mark the edges of tectonic plates
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify practical applications of electromagnetic radiation, such as radio waves used in telecommunications, and x-rays and gamma rays in medicine
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that earthquake epicenters mark tectonic plate boundaries. It contains no information about electromagnetic radiation or its practical applications (radio waves, x-rays, gamma rays in medicine).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Epicenters mark the edges of tectonic plates
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses earthquake epicenters and plate tectonics, not electromagnetic waves, their wavelengths, or frequencies. No support for comparing EM wave types.

copy.en:
Why do scientists care where earthquake epicenters are located?

Epicenters mark the edges of tectonic plates, so mapping them helps scientists see exactly where one plate ends and another begins.
copy.tl:
Bakit mahalaga kung saan matatagpuan ang mga earthquake epicenter?

Ang mga epicenter ay nagmamarka sa mga gilid ng tectonic plates, kaya ang pagmapa sa mga ito ay tumutulong sa mga siyentista na makita kung saan eksaktong nagtatapos ang isang plate at nagsisimula ang isa pa.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga importante sa mga siyentista kon asa nahimutang ang mga earthquake epicenter?

Ang mga epicenter nagmarka sa mga kilid sa tectonic plates, busa ang pagmapa kanila makatabang sa mga siyentista nga makita kon asa eksakto nga mahuman ang usa ka plate ug magsugod ang lain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The East African Rift is a divergent boundary on land where the African continent is slowly splitting apart.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a geological divergent plate boundary, which is unrelated to the competency about describing wave properties using terms like amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity. No instructional support for the physics concept is present.

copy.en: The East African Rift is an example of a continental rift valley formed at a divergent boundary.
copy.tl: Ang East African Rift ay isang halimbawa ng continental rift valley na nabuo sa divergent boundary.
copy.bis: Ang East African Rift usa ka pananglitan sa continental rift valley nga naporma sa divergent boundary.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An eclipse is a shadow in space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of ions as either the loss or gain of electrons to produce ionic bonds, using examples, such as the formation of sodium chloride
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains eclipses as shadows caused by the Moon or Earth blocking sunlight. It contains no information about ion formation, electron loss/gain, or ionic bonds, which are the focus of G9-M-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An eclipse is a shadow in space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about astronomical shadows (eclipses) and does not address subatomic particles, their symbols, mass, charge, or location within an atom, which are the focus of G8-M-3.

copy.en: An eclipse is a shadow in space caused by the Moon or Earth blocking sunlight from reaching the other body.
copy.tl: Ang eclipse ay isang anino sa kalawakan na sanhi ng pagharang ng Buwan o Earth sa sikat ng araw upang hindi ito makarating sa isa pang katawan.
copy.bis: Ang eclipse usa ka anino sa kawanangan nga gipahinabo sa pagbabag sa Bulan o Earth sa silaw sa adlaw aron dili kini makaabot sa laing lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because an ecosystem includes both biotic factors, the living things, and abiotic factors, the nonliving things like water, soil, and sunlight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains ecosystem composition (biotic and abiotic factors) and has no content about forces, movement of objects, or factors affecting motion. It does not support the G3-F-2 competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because an ecosystem includes both biotic factors, the living things, and abiotic factors, the nonliving things like water, soil, and sunlight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the Particle Model of Matter as 'All matter is made up of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles.'
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about ecosystem interactions, not the Particle Model of Matter. It contains no information about particles, pure substances, or the particle nature of matter.

copy.en:
Why do we say an ecosystem is more than just the animals and plants?

Because an ecosystem includes both biotic factors, the living things, and abiotic factors, the nonliving things like water, soil, and sunlight, all interacting with each other!
copy.tl:
Bakit natin sinasabing ang ecosystem ay higit pa sa mga hayop at halaman?

Dahil kasama sa ecosystem ang biotic factors, ang mga may buhay, at abiotic factors, ang mga walang buhay tulad ng tubig, lupa, at sikat ng araw, na lahat ay nakikipag-ugnayan sa isa't isa!
copy.bis:
Ngano man nga giingon nato nga ang ecosystem labaw pa sa mga mananap ug tanom?

Tungod kay ang ecosystem naglakip sa biotic factors, ang mga buhing butang, ug abiotic factors, ang mga dili buhing butang sama sa tubig, yuta, ug kahayag sa adlaw, nga ang tanan mag-uban sa usag usa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Excessive exposure to ionizing radiation can alter molecules within cells and may cause eventual harm such as skin or tissue damage, cancer, and death.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses health effects of ionizing radiation, which has no connection to plate boundary structures, movements, or events.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Excessive exposure to ionizing radiation can alter molecules within cells and may cause eventual harm such as skin or tissue damage, cancer, and death.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about radiation harm, not about subduction of oceanic plates or its impact on the overriding plate.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Excessive exposure to ionizing radiation can alter molecules within cells and may cause eventual harm such as skin or tissue damage, cancer, and death.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card is unrelated to volcano types, activity, eruption type, or crustal location.

copy.en: Excessive exposure to ionizing radiation can alter molecules within cells and may cause eventual harm such as skin or tissue damage, cancer, and death.
copy.tl: Ang labis na pagkakalantad sa ionizing radiation ay maaaring magbago ng mga molecules sa loob ng cells at magdulot ng pinsala tulad ng pagkasira ng balat o tissue, cancer, at kamatayan.
copy.bis: Ang sobra nga pagkaladlad sa ionizing radiation makausab sa mga molecules sa sulod sa cells ug makapahinabo sa kadaot sama sa pagkadaot sa panit o tissue, cancer, ug kamatayon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Komodo dragons, butterflies, salamanders, salmon, and ducks are oviparous animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes oviparous animal reproduction, which is unrelated to identifying volcano locations or assessing eruption risk. No content supports the G6-E-2 competency.

copy.en: Komodo dragons, butterflies, salamanders, salmon, and ducks are oviparous animals, meaning they lay eggs and their young hatch from those eggs.
copy.tl: Ang mga Komodo dragon, paru-paro, salamander, salmon, at itik ay mga oviparous na hayop, ibig sabihin nangingitlog sila at ang kanilang anak ay napipisa mula sa mga itlog na iyon.
copy.bis: Ang mga Komodo dragon, alibangbang, salamander, salmon, ug itik kay mga oviparous nga mananap, nagpasabot nga mangitlog sila ug ang ilang mga anak mapusa gikan sa mga itlog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ovulation occurs when a mature egg, called an ovum, is released from the ovarian follicle into the nearest fallopian tube.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The competency G6-E-7 concerns demonstrating Earth's rotation on its axis to explain day and night. The card describes ovulation, a human reproductive process, which is entirely unrelated to Earth science or day/night cycles.

copy.en: Ovulation occurs when a mature egg, called an ovum, is released from the ovarian follicle into the nearest fallopian tube.
copy.tl: Ang ovulation ay nangyayari kapag ang mature na itlog, na tinatawag na ovum, ay inilalabas mula sa ovarian follicle papunta sa pinakamalapit na fallopian tube.
copy.bis: Ang ovulation mahitabo kung ang mature nga itlog, nga gitawag og ovum, ipagawas gikan sa ovarian follicle ngadto sa labing duol nga fallopian tube.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gas particles are in constant, perfectly elastic motion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the elastic motion of gas particles, a physics/chemistry concept. G5-E-11 is about the structure of the solar system and celestial objects, which is entirely unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gas particles are in constant, perfectly elastic motion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes gas particle motion, not natural objects in the sky. G3-E-6 concerns observing and describing the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars, which is unrelated to this content.

copy.en: Gas particles are in constant, perfectly elastic motion - they bounce off each other and container walls without losing any movement energy.
copy.tl: Ang gas particles ay palaging gumagalaw sa perfectly elastic motion - nagbabanggaan sila sa isa't isa at sa dingding ng container nang hindi nawawalan ng energy ng paggalaw.
copy.bis: Ang gas particles kanunay nga naglihok sa perfectly elastic motion - magbangga sila sa usag-usa ug sa bungbong sa container nga dili mawad-an ug energy sa paglihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electric current is the net flow of electrons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains electric current, a physics concept. It does not address physical vs. chemical changes, reversibility, or irreversibility, which are the focus of G6-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electric current is the net flow of electrons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about electric current, not about changes in solid materials (shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, cutting) or their usefulness. No instructional support for G3-M-8.

copy.en: Electric current is the net flow of electrons, tiny charged particles, moving through a wire like water flowing through a hose.
copy.tl: Ang electric current ay ang net flow ng mga electron, maliliit na charged particles, na dumadaloy sa wire tulad ng tubig na dumadaloy sa hose.
copy.bis: Ang electric current mao ang net flow sa mga electron, gagmay nga charged particles, nga nag-agos sa wire sama sa tubig nga nag-agos sa hose.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the attraction or repulsion between charged objects
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines electric force, a physics concept about charged objects. G7-L-2 requires using a microscope to observe and identify cell parts (cell membrane, nucleus, etc.). There is no connection to cells, microscopy, or living things.

copy.en:
What do you call the push or pull between electric charges?

It is called electric force, the attraction or repulsion between charged objects.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa pagtulak o paghila sa pagitan ng mga electric charges?

Ito ay tinatawag na electric force, ang pag-akit o pagtataboy sa pagitan ng mga charged objects.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tawag sa pagduso o pagbira tali sa mga electric charges?

Kini gitawag nga electric force, ang pag-uyon o pagduso tali sa mga charged objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electrical energy is the most used energy because it is easy to move through wires and can power many appliances at once.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses electrical energy and its transmission, with no mention of chemical reactions, combustion, acids, photosynthesis, respiration, or environmental impacts of chemical reactions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electrical energy is the most used energy because it is easy to move through wires and can power many appliances at once.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card contains no information about acids, bases, salts, or indicators; it is about electrical energy, not chemistry.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electrical energy is the most used energy because it is easy to move through wires and can power many appliances at once.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address local community issues, waste treatment, or how science addresses community concerns; it is a general statement about electrical energy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electrical energy is carried by moving electrons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains electrical energy carried by moving electrons, which is unrelated to the water cycle and its role in the environment. The assigned competency G5-E-6 concerns the water cycle, so the tag is incorrect.

copy.en: Electrical energy is carried by moving electrons, tiny particles inside wires, and it is what lights bulbs and runs appliances.
copy.tl: Ang electrical energy ay dala ng mga gumagalaw na electron, maliliit na particle sa loob ng wire, at ito ang nagpapailaw sa bumbilya at nagpapaandar ng mga appliances.
copy.bis: Ang electrical energy gidala sa mga naglihok nga electron, gagmay nga mga partikulo sa sud sa wire, ug kini mao ang nagpasiga sa bombilya ug nagpadagan sa mga appliances.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electricity is a form of energy, and the bright flash of lightning is a natural example of static electricity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: Lightning as static electricity is unrelated to comparing mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the bright flash of lightning is a natural example of static electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Static electricity is unrelated to plant reproduction.

copy.en: Electricity is a form of energy, and the bright flash of lightning is a natural example of static electricity.
copy.tl: Ang electricity ay isang anyo ng enerhiya, at ang maliwanag na kidlat ay natural na halimbawa ng static electricity.
copy.bis: Ang electricity usa ka matang sa enerhiya, ug ang masilaw nga kilat usa ka natural nga pananglitan sa static electricity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electromagnetic induction happens when a conductor, like a wire, moves through a magnetic field and electric charges begin to flow.

copy.bis: Mahitabo ang electromagnetic induction kung ang usa ka conductor, sama sa wire, molihok sa magnetic field ug magsugod sa pag-agos ang mga electric charge.

copy.en:
How can I easily see the valence electrons of an atom?

Draw the element's symbol, then place dots around it to represent its valence electrons!
copy.tl:
Paano ko madaling makikita ang mga valence electron ng isang atom?

Iguhit ang simbolo ng elemento, pagkatapos ay lagyan ng mga tuldok sa paligid nito upang kumatawan sa mga valence electron nito!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nako dali nga makita ang mga valence electron sa usa ka atom?

Idrowing ang simbolo sa elemento, dayon butangi og mga tuldok sa palibot aron magrepresentar sa iyang mga valence electron!

copy.en: Electrons are found in layers around the nucleus called electron shells, which are at different distances from the center.
copy.tl: Ang mga electron ay matatagpuan sa mga patong sa paligid ng nucleus na tinatawag na electron shells, na may iba't ibang distansya mula sa gitna.
copy.bis: Ang mga electron makita sa mga lut-od libot sa nucleus nga gitawag ug electron shells, nga lainlain ang distansya gikan sa tunga.

copy.tl: Ang proteins ay naglalaman ng carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, at sulfur.

copy.en:
Is the extremely low frequency radiation from power lines dangerous?

Most scientists say no! The electric fields at a cell in the body are thousands of times smaller than those from normal electric activity of nearby cells.
copy.tl:
Mapanganib ba ang extremely low frequency radiation mula sa mga power lines?

Karamihan sa mga scientist ay nagsasabing hindi! Ang electric fields sa isang selula sa katawan ay libu-libong beses na mas maliit kaysa sa normal na electric activity ng mga kalapit na selula.
copy.bis:
Delikado ba ang extremely low frequency radiation gikan sa mga power lines?

Kadaghanan sa mga scientist nag-ingon nga dili! Ang electric fields sa usa ka selula sa lawas liboan ka beses nga mas gamay kaysa sa normal nga electric activity sa mga duol nga selula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A microphone is the reverse of a loudspeaker! Sound vibrates a small diaphragm attached to a coil inside a magnetic field, producing a small electrical current that represents the sound.

assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to describe similarities and differences between electric motors and electric generators. The card describes a microphone converting sound to electricity, which is a transducer, not a motor or generator. It does not support the stated skill.

copy.en: A microphone is the reverse of a loudspeaker! Sound vibrates a small diaphragm attached to a coil inside a magnetic field, producing a small electrical current that represents the sound.
copy.tl: Ang mikropono ay kabaligtaran ng loudspeaker! Ang tunog ay nagpapayanig ng maliit na diaphragm na nakakabit sa coil sa loob ng magnetic field, na gumagawa ng maliit na kuryente na nagrerepresenta sa tunog.
copy.bis: Ang mikropono kabaligtaran sa loudspeaker! Ang tunog nagpayanig sa gagmay nga diaphragm nga nakakabit sa usa ka coil sulod sa magnetic field, nagmugna ug gamay nga kuryente nga nagrerepresenta sa tunog.

copy.tl: Ang electromagnetic waves ay may mga kapaki-pakinabang na gamit tulad ng komunikasyon, pagluluto, medical imaging, at pag-sterilize ng pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang electromagnetic waves adunay mapuslanong mga gamit sama sa komunikasyon, pagluto, medical imaging, ug pag-sterilize sa pagkaon.

copy.en:
Why is knowing percentage composition useful?

It helps scientists determine the empirical formula, which is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a substance.
copy.tl:
Bakit kapaki-pakinabang ang pag-alam ng percentage composition?

Nakakatulong ito sa mga scientist na malaman ang empirical formula, na siyang pinakasimpleng whole-number ratio ng mga atom sa isang substance.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mapuslanon ang pagkahibalo sa percentage composition?

Makatabang kini sa mga scientist nga mahibaloan ang empirical formula, nga mao ang pinakasimple nga whole-number ratio sa mga atom sa usa ka substance.

copy.en:
What gives sperm cells the energy to swim?

The seminal vesicle produces a sugar-rich fluid that provides energy for the sperm cells' motility, or movement.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagbibigay ng enerhiya sa sperm cells para lumangoy?

Ang seminal vesicle ay gumagawa ng fluid na mayaman sa asukal na nagbibigay ng enerhiya para sa motility, o paggalaw, ng sperm cells.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghatag ug enerhiya sa sperm cells aron molangoy?

Ang seminal vesicle naghimo ug fluid nga dato sa asukal nga naghatag ug enerhiya alang sa motility, o paglihok, sa sperm cells.

copy.en: Chemical potential energy is stored inside chemical bonds, the tiny attractive forces that hold atoms together in things like batteries and food.
copy.tl: Ang chemical potential energy ay nakaimbak sa loob ng chemical bonds, ang maliliit na pwersang humihila at nagdidikit sa mga atom sa mga bagay tulad ng baterya at pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang chemical potential energy gitipigan sa sulod sa chemical bonds, ang gagmay nga pwersa nga mobira ug mopilit sa mga atomo sa mga butang sama sa baterya ug pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: energy remains constant and is neither created nor destroyed

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes conservation of energy in an isolated system. G8-F-1 is about forces causing acceleration and acceleration as rate of change of velocity. The card contains no information about forces, acceleration, or velocity, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: In an isolated system, where nothing enters or leaves, energy remains constant and is neither created nor destroyed, only changing from one form to another.
copy.tl: Sa isang isolated system, kung saan walang pumapasok o lumalabas, ang energy ay nananatiling pareho at hindi nalilikha o nasisira, nagbabago lang ito mula sa isang anyo papunta sa iba.
copy.bis: Sa usa ka isolated system, diin walay mosulod o mogawas, ang energy magpabilin nga pareho ug dili malalang o malaglag, mausab lang kini gikan sa usa ka porma ngadto sa lain.

copy.en:
What happens when greenhouse gas concentrations rise in the atmosphere?

A greater amount of infrared light is absorbed and less escapes straight into space, causing an enhanced warming phenomenon.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag tumaas ang konsentrasyon ng greenhouse gases sa atmosphere?

Mas maraming infrared light ang naa-absorb at mas kaunti ang direktang nakalalabas sa space, kaya nagdudulot ng enhanced warming phenomenon.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mahitabo kon mosaka ang konsentrasyon sa greenhouse gases sa atmosphere?

Mas daghan nga infrared light ang ma-absorb ug mas menos ang direktang makagawas sa space, mao nga nagpahinabo ug enhanced warming phenomenon.

copy.bis: Kon moabot sa kinatas-ang lebel ang estrogen, magsenyas kini sa utok nga magpagawas ug LH, ug kining pagsaka sa LH maoy hinungdan sa ovulation.
